reads_as_reason: Both sheets show the same blocky figure: a boxy head with almost no neck, a squared chest slab, shoulders much wider than the reference outlines, and straight uniform limbs. That reads as a toy or mannequin, not a sleek adult humanoid.

G1.evidence: Front silhouette: head is a rounded-square block sitting directly on a slab-like chest. Metrics list neck length as FAIL (P2a 0.1143 hu) and shoulder width as FAIL (P3 0.418 against a band of 0.22-0.29). The torso is a rounded box with a horizontal dark band across the waist. This reads as a character or toy proportion.

G2.evidence: Equal-height lineup: the chest-waist-pelvis flow is broken. The chest is a block, a dark waist band cuts it off, and the pelvis is a separate squat box. Arms and legs are near-constant-width tubes cut into stacked segments by dark bands. Metrics agree: thigh and shank taper fail (P8a 0.8108, P8b 0.8639), and calf widest point is too low (P9b 0.3933). The dark joint bands are deliberate recesses, but they mark off blocks instead of joining flowing forms.

G3.evidence: Two-tone view: matte white shells, graphite joint bands, hands and boots, and a gloss-black visor, with no second accent colour. The back view is fully shelled in white. The ragged black/white edge at the knee in the side view and at the lower torso in the three-quarter view looks like a material-assignment artefact, not a design choice.

G4.evidence: Head, chest, pelvis, arm and leg segments share the same squarish, small-radius rounded-box section, so the radii family is consistent. That consistency is what makes the figure look boxy. The thick arm tubes with 45-degree-looking ends are the one segment that departs from the rest.

G6.evidence: At equal height the candidate does not read as family with optimus_like or atlas_like. Matching: head height and hip and knee heights (P1, P6, P7 pass), and a graphite visor and dark joints in the two-tone. Not matching: shoulders and arms are far wider and more splayed, the neck is almost absent, there is no waist or torso taper, the legs are fat and straight with no calf shaping, and the foot is long (P10a 0.238 against a band of 0.13-0.17). S2 IoU is 0.5332 against optimus_like and 0.5657 against atlas_like.

pairwise.evidence: Weak preference, low confidence. The studio shading and silhouettes of A5 (baseline, Image A) and A9 (candidate, Image B) are almost identical, and neither fixes the toy proportions. The candidate looks slightly more finished in the two-tone: the back view is fully white-shelled where the baseline back is an unassigned flat grey, the hands and boots are graphite, and the arms are consistent white shells with dark joint bands. The candidate also has a longer foot and a blotchy dark patch at the knee side that the baseline lacks. Those are small negatives against a clearer two-tone read.

top_changes.change: Narrow the shoulders and arm block so the outer shoulder width falls toward the 0.22-0.29 H band (now 0.418). Pull the arm roots inward and reduce the A-pose splay. This is the largest single gap to both references.

Add a visible neck: lower the chest top or raise the head so the visible neck reaches the 0.18-0.55 hu band (now 0.1143 hu). Keep the neck at least 0.5 of head width. Round the head section toward a capsule or ovoid rather than a box.

Taper the legs: make the thigh distal section about 65% of the proximal area (now 0.81) and the ankle about 60% of the calf area (now 0.86). Move the calf's widest point up to within 33% of the shank length from the top (now 0.39). Shorten the foot toward 0.13-0.17 H (now 0.238).

notes: The studio clay views and the two-tone views are the same geometry for baseline and candidate. The differences between them are small and I could not isolate their cause from the images. I did not estimate any ratios; all numbers come from the candidate's design_metrics.json, and there is no baseline metrics file, so I cannot compare numerics between A5 and A9. I judged the speckled boundaries in the two-tone render as likely render artefacts, not design flaws. The side-view silhouette shows a long foot and a box-like backpack protrusion; I did not judge the backpack as a separate item.
